title: Registered correlations, official numbers only, each with n
rule: Computed only from numbers printed on an official nfl.com page that this workspace read. Each value carries n, a two-sided p (normal approximation of the t test, disclosed) and a Fisher-z 95% interval. No market, price, prop or third-party number is used.

computed.name: Home margin vs game total
computed.reading: Home margin and total are nearly orthogonal on this sample.
computed.note: computed from nfl-sources/data/results.json, whose rows each cite their official week page

computed.name: A club's points scored, consecutive games
computed.reading: A small positive autocorrelation: last week's scoring barely predicts this week's. n counts ordered pairs of games, not games.

computed.name: Points scored vs points allowed, same game (club-game level)
computed.reading: A negative value means a game's two scores are not independent draws — the obvious reading is pace. This is the number that makes 'just multiply the probabilities' wrong for prop combos in the same game.
computed.note: n counts club-games (two per game), because the observation is a club's scoring and conceding

computed.name: Rest-day differential (home minus away) vs home margin
computed.inputs: official final scores + the dates printed on the official week pages (no schedule date is taken from anywhere else)
computed.reading: Week-1 games are excluded because neither club has a previous game in the corpus. Rest is derived from printed dates, so a rescheduled game would show up here as a rest anomaly rather than being smoothed away.

computed.name: International game (printed section) vs home margin
computed.inputs: official final scores + the section heading printed on the official week page
computed.reading: n = 8 international games is far too small to estimate a home-field effect, so no correlation is printed: a point-biserial r on this split would be noise dressed as a number. The group means are shown with their n and nothing is concluded from them.
